name: MiaraOS
description: A calm, private baby-care log for everyone who cares for your baby. Feeds, sleep, diapers, growth and first foods take a tap, or a sentence to Siri, Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini. Your partner sees it the moment it’s saved.
facts: Native iOS and Android apps with Live Activities and widgets
Conversational logging through Siri and a remote MCP server
Shared households with roles for parents and caregivers

images.alt: Three iPhones showing the MiaraOS Trends, Today and Timeline screens under the headline "Every feed, diaper and nap, shared."
MiaraOS app icon: a serif M with a clay dot on cream
A MiaraOS household of two parents, a caregiver and a viewer, above a feed of entries showing who logged or edited each one, including a bottle logged via Claude
MiaraOS Lock Screen live activities for a nap timer and a nursing session
MiaraOS in dark mode: the diaper sheet with one-tap Wet, Dirty and Mixed buttons and the time filled in, over a running sleep timer
The MiaraOS Today screen in dark mode: time since the last feed, diaper and wake-up, with today's totals beside the typical range for age
The MiaraOS day timeline in dark mode, laying out a night of sleep, a 3:19 AM bottle and diaper changes hour by hour

features.title: One tap, then back to bed
features.body: Diapers take a single tap; bottles, nursing and sleep take a few, with the time already filled in. Or just say “log a 5 oz bottle.”

features.title: Everyone in sync at handoff
features.body: Invite a partner, grandparent or nanny. The night shift sees what the day shift logged the moment it’s saved, and every entry shows who added or changed it.

features.title: The nap keeps time
features.body: Sleep and nursing timers live on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. Whoever is up can end them from their own phone.

features.title: Answers at 3 AM
features.body: Today shows how long since the last feed, diaper and sleep, beside the typical range for age. The timeline lays out the whole night, hour by hour.

oneLiner: A calm baby log the whole household shares, in a tap.

name: NameWise
tagline: Baby names, picked for you. Chosen together.
description: An AI naming assistant for expecting couples. It learns your style, roots and must-haves, deals name cards that explain why they fit, and sharpens with every swipe. Match on a first name, then find the middle that flows.
facts: Partners swipe independently; mutual likes become matches, with a push to your partner
Every card shows a match score, meaning and why it fits; swipes and notes tune the next batch
Name library, Middle Name Explorer and private family swiping

images.alt: Three iPhones showing the NameWise library, a swipe card for the name Lucia and a match screen, under "Find the name, together"
NameWise app icon: a cream serif N with a rose dot on sage green
NameWise onboarding: choosing which name styles feel right
A NameWise name card: Lucía, 96% match, meaning "Light", with a line on why it fits the classic, nature feel you described
The NameWise match screen: "It's a match! Lucía. Sam Rivera loved this name too!"
The NameWise Name Library: Rowan and Maeve loved, a saved note on Rowan, and the partner who liked each name
A NameWise middle-name card: Rowan Elena Rivera, 92% match, "Elena flows well between Rowan and Rivera"

features.title: It asks before it suggests
features.body: A few short questions on style, roots, meaning and popularity, plus the names you already love. Must-haves, like a starting letter, are rules, not hints.

features.title: Every card makes its case
features.body: Each name comes with a match score, its meaning and a line on why it fits you. Love, like, pass or add a note, and the next batch gets sharper.

features.title: Swipe apart, match together
features.body: You each swipe privately. When you both love a name, it's a match, and your partner gets a push. Every like lands in your library with notes and matches.

features.title: Then, the middle name
features.body: Lock in a first name and NameWise suggests middles scored on how the full name sounds with your surname. Swipe them the same way, together.

oneLiner: An AI baby-name finder you swipe through together until you match.

name: WeWatch
description: A shared watchlist for two. Each partner picks favorites and describes their taste; Claude blends both into fresh picks every week, says why you'll like each one, and shows where it's streaming.
facts: Recommendations that blend two people's taste
IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes scores with streaming badges
Native SwiftUI (Liquid Glass) and Android apps

images.alt: WeWatch: "What to watch, together." in a large editorial serif on a dark cinematic gradient
The WeWatch homepage on a phone
WeWatch app icon: a glass TV with sparkles over a magenta, indigo and teal gradient

features.title: Two tastes, one list
features.body: Each of you picks favorites and writes what you love. Claude blends both into weekly picks, and when tonight calls for something lighter, one sentence reshuffles the list.

features.title: One list, every screen
features.body: Native SwiftUI on iPhone with Liquid Glass, Kotlin on Android, and the web, all sharing one list. Every poster carries IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes scores and streaming badges.

oneLiner: A shared watchlist that blends two tastes into picks you’ll both love.

name: Semester.ly
tagline: Every schedule that fits, built for you.
description: The course scheduler I co-founded at Johns Hopkins. Pick your classes and it builds every conflict-free schedule, with ratings, reviews and open seats a click away. Open source since 2017, it still plans Hopkins semesters.
facts: 1,000+ Hopkins users in its first 24 hours
2M+ searches across nearly a dozen universities
Open source since 2017, now run by JHU Open Source

images.alt: A generated Hopkins week in Semester.ly: Linear Algebra, Calculus III, Physics, Data Structures and Intermediate Programming, with dots to flip between schedule options
The Data Structures course card: 4 credits, a four-star average rating, classmates' emoji reactions, prerequisites and past evaluations by term
Advanced Search filtering by department, area, level and day/time
The Semester.ly shield logo and wordmark over a faded schedule
The Semester.ly shield logo in coral, teal, sky blue and yellow

features.title: Every schedule that fits
features.body: Add your courses and it builds every conflict-free week. Flip through the options, then lock the sections you can't move.

features.title: Know the class first
features.body: One click shows the average rating, past evaluations by term, prerequisites and how classmates really felt, in emoji.

features.title: Search the whole catalog
features.body: Filter by department, area, level and time to find the class that fits the hole in your week.

oneLiner: The conflict-free course scheduler I co-founded at Johns Hopkins.

name: Fitbit Dual-Wear Compare
tagline: Two trackers. Know which to trust.
description: For anyone wearing two or three trackers at once. Connect Fitbit, Strava, Polar or Oura accounts, pick a day, and heart rate, steps, sleep and workouts line up on one timeline, with the disagreements flagged and scored.

images.alt: Heart-rate card overlaying a full day from two devices: a low overnight trace, a walk, a sharp lunch-run peak and an evening yoga bump, with two red High BPM Error bands, averages of 68 and 69 and a PE10 of 2.36%
Sleep Stages Agreement card stacking two devices' awake, light, deep and REM timelines, with a 70% agreement rate and a 5.3% sleep duration delta

Activity Summary comparing the same 12:05 lunch run from two devices, with distance, calories, elevation, heart-rate PE10 and cross-track error deltas above overlaid heart-rate traces where the second device is slow to lock on and briefly reads high

features.title: Every beat, overlaid
features.body: Minute-by-minute heart rate from each device on one chart. Red bands mark where they split, and PE10 scores how often they land more than 10 bpm apart.

features.title: Sleep, stage by stage
features.body: Each device’s night stacked as a hypnogram. The agreement rate shows how often both called the same stage; the duration delta is the gap in total sleep.

features.title: Run against run
features.body: Pick a workout from each device to see distance, calories, elevation and route error side by side, with heart rate overlaid. Pair a Polar strap and it becomes ground truth.

oneLiner: Wear two trackers at once and see which one to trust.
